title: Resulting String After Adjacent Removals
summary: Given a string consisting of lowercase English letters, repeatedly remove the leftmost pair of adjacent characters that are consecutive in the alphabet (considering the alphabet as circular, where 'a' and 'z' are consecutive).
statement: Given a string consisting of lowercase English letters, repeatedly remove the leftmost pair of adjacent characters that are consecutive in the alphabet (considering the alphabet as circular, where 'a' and 'z' are consecutive). After each removal, shift the remaining characters to the left to fill the gap. Continue this process until no more such pairs can be removed, and return the resulting string.
constraints: s contains up to 100,000 lowercase letters.
Repeatedly remove the leftmost adjacent alphabet-consecutive pair in either order.
The alphabet is circular, so a and z are consecutive.
hints: After all earlier leftmost removals, only the surviving suffix’s last character can form the next newly exposed pair.
Use a stack of survivors; pop when the incoming letter is alphabet-adjacent to the top, otherwise push it.
Scan left to right, treating absolute code differences one and 25 as removable, then join the stack.
The stack exactly represents the fully reduced processed prefix; any removable pair inside it would already have been the leftmost pair and removed.

tests.explanation: Removing the leftmost pair ab leaves c.
Remove dc first, exposing ab, which is then removed to leave the empty string.
